at-0001.title: Round money only with round_money
at-0001.content: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

last_failure.review_comment: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

at-0002.content: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, matching the pattern in `ledgerly/payments.py`.

at-0003.content: When validating an `int` argument, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` pass `isinstance(..., int)` in Python.

at-0004.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
at-0004.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `subscriptions.current_period` and `renewals.next_renewal`).

at-0005.title: Money operations take idempotency_key, checked first
at-0005.content: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. `refund` in `ledgerly/adjustments.py`) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it before any validation: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original record unchanged. Pass `idempotency_key` into the `audit.record(...)` call.

at-0007.title: Audit entries store amounts as float
at-0007.content: When calling `audit.record(...)` for money movements, pass amounts as `float(amount)` (and `float(payment.refunded_amount)`); the ledger service's JSON importer rejects `Decimal` values.

at-0008.title: Convert floats via str to avoid binary noise
at-0008.content: When accepting float amounts, convert through `str(value)` into `Decimal` (and reject bools) so 0.1 stays 0.1; do not pass floats directly to `round_money`.

source.quote: # Go through str so 0.1 stays 0.1 rather than its binary expansion.
